mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the FEDFUNDS decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of the triggered instances despite the UNRATE decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals increased economic output, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the INDPRO increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of the instances following a sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the inflationary pressure and tight monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the weakening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) also decrease by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a significant economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 quarters and RSAFS decreases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the economic contraction.
